subject: EdgeCraft preflight: on‑prem cluster runbook + routing & storage constraints
messages:
From: Nolan Baxter <nolan@edgecraft.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@edgecraft.ai
Date: 2029-12-01T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: On‑prem preflight: hardware inventory + routing constraints

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for taking this. As discussed, we pulled together the high‑level inventory and the current routing/egress constraints for the Salt Lake City site. Two quick callouts up front: the site is semi‑isolated (limited internet egress via a single NAT gateway) and the on‑prem team wants the ability to pin certain pods to NVMe nodes for low latency.

Attachments: edgecraft_site_inventory_v3.csv, edgecraft_network_diagram_v2.pdf

Summary/highlights (see attachments for details):
- Hardware: 6x racked hosts (2x A100/80GB per host), 2x storage servers with 100TB usable (NFS export), local NVMe on nodes for /scratch
- Networking: single public egress (NAT), internal VLANs for infra/tenant traffic, no BGP peering to cloud; limited outbound to our partner IP allowlist only
- Compliance: logs must be retained 180 days, KMS integration preferred but we can provide a hardware HSM if required
- Ops ask: prefer Redwood to propose node classes + storage mapping and call out any functionality that will require alternative routing (e.g., metrics export, telemetry, KV cache warming)

Would you be able to send an initial nodepool + storage mapping recommendation and note any gating items (CSI drivers, CNI constraints, firewall ports)? We'd like that before the procurement PO.

Also copying procurement (procure@edgecraft.ai) so they see the inventory attachments.

Best,
Nolan
Head of Infrastructure, EdgeCraft

Nolan —

Thanks for the inventory and diagram, that helps. Quick read and initial asks below; I'll follow up with a short proposed mapping doc (attached) and a 30‑minute technical call slot for Wednesday.

Quick clarifications:
- Is the NAT egress single IP fixed or behind a floating VIP? (we may need static egress for our metrics/telemetry endpoints)
- Do you have a preferred CSI driver (currently we support local‑nvme + rook/ceph + nfs‑server external)?
- For KMS/HSM: do you plan to manage keys in your HSM or shall Redwood integrate to a customer KMS via mutual TLS?

Initial recommendations (high level):
1) Node classes:
   - gpu-hot (A100 hosts) — pinned workloads, local NVMe for model KV cache (scratch)
   - gpu-batch — same hosts, tainted for async batch only, smaller pod density
   - storage-backend — storage servers serving NFS for long term artifacts and logs
   - infra — control plane/monitoring/tracing on separate VLAN (small cores)

2) Storage mapping:
   - model KV/cache -> local NVMe (ephemeral, snapshot to NFS nightly)
   - artifacts/diagnostics -> NFS (encrypted at rest on host)
   - metrics & logs -> push to a pull endpoint on our collector; if egress is restricted we can run a local aggregator and ship on schedule

3) Networking & routing: open ports 443 outbound to our collector IPs, TCP 22 only from admin VLAN, and kube control plane ports (6443) between infra and control plane only. We will provide firewall rule set.

I've attached a short nodeclass recommendation PDF (redwood_k8s_nodeclass_recs.pdf) and proposed call times. Can Marissa and Irene join the Wednesday call? They will own storage and rollout respectively.

—Avery
Private Deploy Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks — looping in a few technical specifics we should lock before PO/SOW:

1) CSI & persistent patterns
- We'll recommend using the vendor NFS for long‑term volumes via the standard NFS CSI driver (mount options will include noac and data=ordered where supported).
- For model KV caches we will use local NVMe as emptyDir on gpu‑hot nodes, plus nightly rsync to NFS for crash recovery (note: this makes model cold restarts slower but keeps hot path fast).

2) KV cache durability and recompute
- If you want near‑zero warmup after failover we need a small persistent cache tier (10–20GB) on the NFS exported volume per nodegroup. That will add complexity and lockfiles; confirm if acceptable.

3) Security — KMS/HSM
- We support mTLS to customer KMS endpoints. Our control plane will store only wrapped keys; HSM signing operations can remain local at EdgeCraft. We'll include a KMS integration runbook for ops.

4) Network telemetry & egress
- Because egress is single IP, we'll add a pull model for metrics (grafana agent configured to poll local aggregator) and a scheduled push window (daily) for heavyweight telemetry.

5) RBAC & node isolation
- We'll surface a nodeAffinity-based tenancy model (dedicated service accounts for inference pods) and restrict kubelet access to the infra VLAN.

Action items:
- Nolan: confirm whether small persistent cache (10–20GB per GPU nodegroup) is acceptable; if not we'll scope increased warmup on restart.
- Avery: add the KMS integration runbook link into the SOW (Irene please append).
- Karthik: please produce a short firewall ruleset (ports + IPs) we can hand to EdgeCraft network team.

If everyone agrees, we can attach these callouts to the SOW and send for signature.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
